brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Fennick Outdoor. Over the weekend the distribution center replaced its edge router. Its two HA VPN tunnels to prod-vpc show ESTABLISHED, but since 06:30 nothing in the center can reach the warehouse system in Google Cloud. The morning shift starts scanning at 08:00.
handover: The network team's change record: new edge router, new BGP ASN 65010 (old router used 65001), same link-local addresses and MD5 keys.
Cloud Router cr-dc (ASN 64520) has peers dc-peer-0 and dc-peer-1 configured with peer ASN 65001.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the distribution center's new router, the two tunnels, the BGP sessions and the routes they carry.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the center lost access with tunnels up, what you changed, and how router changes are checked now.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: Both tunnels were ESTABLISHED, but both BGP sessions were down: the new edge router sent ASN 65010 and cr-dc's peers expected 65001 ('bad peer AS'). With no sessions, Cloud Router learned no routes.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Updated dc-peer-0 and dc-peer-1 to peer ASN 65010; both came up with 12 routes. Recreating the gateway would have changed its IPs and broken the tunnels too.

parts.label: Checked now
parts.modelAnswer: Edge router changes now include the cloud peers' ASN, link-local addresses and keys with a cloud reviewer, and BGP session down alerts.

expertPath.text: Both peers DOWN with 0 routes; 'bad peer AS 65010, expected 65001'; tunnels ESTABLISHED; change record assumed no cloud change.

newIps.headline: Fix the layer that failed
newIps.body: IPsec was up; BGP was down with a clear error. Change the peer ASN; rebuilding the gateway only adds a second outage.

shiftDown.headline: Tunnels up is not routes up
shiftDown.body: HA VPN carries routes over BGP. With the sessions down, the VPC has no route to the center even though the tunnels are established.

peered.headline: Good: read the BGP error
peered.body: You separated IPsec from BGP, read the OPEN error, matched the peer ASN to the new router on both peers, checked routes and the app, and closed the gap in the change process.

scoring.modelReasoning: The tunnels are up but both BGP sessions are down, so no routes are exchanged; the router logs say the peer presents ASN 65010 while Cloud Router expects 65001, which matches the weekend's router change. Update the peer ASN on both BGP peers and check routes and the app. Recreating the gateway changes its IPs and adds an outage; resetting tunnels does nothing for BGP. Fix the change process and alert on BGP sessions.
